findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses bogus computed keys, so sync-mode parsing removes every field except access_token.
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]". Both computed entries collapse into that one key, with the second definition winning. The schema is effectively `{ access_token, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. zod's default object parsing strips unknown keys, so with credential sync on, `expiry_date`, `expires_in` and every other field the sync endpoint returns is dropped. For example, Zoom's `newTokens.expires_in` becomes undefined, so the expiry is computed as NaN. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()`, or a `catchall(z.unknown())`, and validate the expiry field explicitly.

findings.title: In sync mode the fetch Response has no `.data`, so Google token refresh crashes.
findings.body: When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and the sync endpoint are set, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch `Response`. `res?.data` is then undefined, and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError, so Google Calendar can never refresh in sync mode. The Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM callers (`tokenInfo.data.error`, `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`) fail the same way, because they expect an axios response. Either have `refreshOAuthTokens` return parsed JSON in a shape each caller adapts, or adapt each caller to read `await response.json()` in sync mode.

findings.title: Google credential key is overwritten with the SafeParseResult wrapper instead of the token data.
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod `SafeParseResult` (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed object. The old code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which is the data. Now `key` is `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, and that is written to `credential.key`. The next time the credential is loaded, `access_token` and `refresh_token` are missing at the top level, so the Google integration breaks after its first token refresh. Use `const parsed = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...); if (!parsed.success) throw ...; const key = parsed.data;`.

findings.title: In sync mode HubSpot treats the raw fetch Response as a token and saves it as the credential key.
findings.body: With sync enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch `Response`, not a `HubspotToken`. `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` is undefined, so `expiryDate` becomes NaN, and the Response object itself is written to `credential.key`. That destroys the stored HubSpot credential. Parse the JSON body and map it to the `HubspotToken` shape before saving.

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes on every client build, throws on an empty statusText, and never uses the new token.
findings.body: `getClient` now does a refresh-token exchange every time the service is constructed. The `response.statusText !== "OK"` check throws on any response whose status text is not literally "OK", including every HTTP/2 response, where the status text is empty. That would make Salesforce unusable. The new token is saved, but the `jsforce.Connection` is still built from the old `credentialKey.access_token`. The request also bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync does not apply here. Check `response.ok`, refresh only when needed, and build the connection from `accessTokenParsed.data`. I could not confirm from the shown hunks whether `prisma` is imported in this file.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects the user id.
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` sends this argument to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId`, while every other integration passes `credential.userId`. The sync endpoint will return tokens for whatever user happens to have that id, which can be another user's tokens, or nothing. Pass the credential's `userId`.

findings.title: A placeholder "refresh_token" can overwrite the real stored refresh token.
findings.body: This placeholder is set whenever the parsed data has no `refresh_token`, even when sync is off. Office 365 then spreads the parsed data over the stored credentials (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`). If `refreshTokenResponseSchema` does not include `refresh_token` (zod strips it), the real refresh token is replaced by the literal string "refresh_token" and saved. Every refresh after that fails. I could not see the Office schema to confirm. Only add a placeholder in sync mode, and never let it override an existing stored token.

findings.title: The webhook secret is compared with plain `!==`, which leaks timing.
findings.body: This endpoint lets the caller write OAuth credentials for any user id, but it authenticates with a plain string comparison. That comparison is open to timing attacks, and an array-valued header is never handled. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers, and reject the request if the header is not a single string.

findings.title: The sync request is unauthenticated and its HTTP status is never checked.
findings.body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no secret or signature. The self-hoster's endpoint cannot tell Cal.com apart from anyone else, so it ends up handing live OAuth access tokens to any caller who supplies a user id. Send the shared webhook secret (or an HMAC) in a header, as the inbound webhook does. A non-2xx response is also returned as if it were a success; check `response.ok`.

findings.title: An invalid Office 365 token response now throws, and the merge can still store the SafeParseResult.
findings.body: An invalid token response used to be logged, and the existing credentials were kept. Now `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws, and the error logging that included the MS response was removed. The surviving `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` spread is only partly reachable, and in sync mode it merges the stripped minimum schema (see the schema finding). Decide on one behaviour, and keep diagnostic logging of the failing response.

findings.title: Bad bodies and failed decryption surface as unhandled 500s.
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` throws on an invalid body. `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` throw on a wrong key or a bad payload. All of these escape as unhandled exceptions and produce 500s. Use `safeParse` and try/catch, and return 400 instead.

held.title: The redirect URI was hardcoded instead of using `appConfig.slug`, which the request does not cover.
held.body: Swapping `appConfig.slug` for a hardcoded "zoho-bigin" is unrelated to credential sync. If the slug ever differs, the redirect will stop matching the callback route. Revert it, or explain why it is needed.
